The cited example's clause (a) defines the full four-dimensional diamond, whereas clauses (b)–(c) establish this area only for its section u^2=u^3=0 and boosts along x^1. The event x^{-1}(1,0,1/2,0) belongs to the full diamond and lies outside that section. The page must identify the planar section and the permitted boosts.

The title names '$J^+(p)\\cap J^-(q)$ for $p=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$ and $q=x^{-1}(2,0,0,0)$ and its invariant coordinate area'. This diamond is four-dimensional by Example (a); the proof computes a two-dimensional area only for the section u^2=u^3=0, invariant under boosts in its (0,1) plane. The repaired body supplies these restrictions, but the title still attributes the area to the full diamond.
